A1.justification: Both complete 14-page PDFs describe the same PACT reconstruction study despite the title change. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and supplementary Sections S1–S4 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original reconstruction and ablation results on five numerical phantoms, plus reconstructions of previously collected leaf-phantom and mouse-liver measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and additionally reports measured transducer-response characterization and a calculated system modulation transfer function in Fig. S1.

M1.justification: The pixel-grid and neural-field representations, differentiable wavefront/PSF model, multi-channel deconvolution, loss, and reconstruction procedure remain unchanged. Coordinate-based terminology and the expanded consistency explanation do not introduce a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five numerical phantoms, leaf phantom, and in vivo mouse liver. The added instrument-response characterization concerns the existing acquisition system and introduces no distinct reconstruction task or test environment.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain conventional DAS, Dual-SOS DAS, APACT, and the proposed method's applicable oracle and regularization variants. Table 1's change from DAS to Conventional DAS is a rename, and appendix renumbering preserves comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 changes the reported NF/PG learning rates from 0.1/0.005 to 0.005/0.1. Section S3.2 changes the selected PG weight from lambda > 1e-4 to lambda = 1e-4, matching v3's existing figure caption. These are reported-setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: New Section S1.4 and Fig. S1 characterize the measured electrical impulse response, its frequency spectrum, and the system MTF. This adds a limited instrument-response analysis. The delay-count, TV-weight, network-size, and anatomical-overlay analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain averaging over five numerical phantoms. Neither reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new characterization adds no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 newly reports the band-pass response and ring-structured MTF in Fig. S1. Section 4.1 also corrects APACT's stated runtime from 22 to 23 minutes, matching the unchanged Table 1. Main benchmark values and existing ablation curves are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the straight-ray and isoplanatic assumptions, and the supplementary Fourier-series account remain unchanged. The added consistency explanation and standard PSF/MTF calculations introduce no substantive formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly specify ring-array PACT. The conclusion replaces the proposed extension to 3D PACT with a broader large-scale scalability claim. The central self-supervised reconstruction contributions and claimed 35-fold speedup remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds a mechanism explanation linking SOS errors through path integrals to PSFs across patches and multi-delay consistency. Section S1.4 attributes MTF rings to DAS projection arcs. The conclusion removes the specific discussion of 3D computational challenges and potential extension.

D1.justification: Section S1.4 newly specifies phase-only EIR deconvolution and how the system PSF and MTF are calculated; calibration itself was already disclosed in v3. Hyperparameter descriptions are revised, and the abstract newly states that synthetic phantoms accompany the code on the renamed project page.

R1.justification: v4 removes Chen et al.'s 2024 PATTERN paper alongside the 3D-extension discussion. The remaining cited works and positioning against APACT, supervised learning, and neural-field approaches are retained; subsequent reference-number changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: The title changes from Self-Supervised to Coordinate-based, with localized abstract, method, and conclusion rewrites. Affiliations and contact information change, acknowledgments and an experimental-details subsection are added, and terminology is edited. The overall narrative and section organization remain.

P2.justification: v4 adds the EIR/MTF figure, refreshes the overview illustration, expands the network-size legend and final phantom caption, and adjusts layout. Earlier supplementary Figs. S1–S4 become S2–S5 with their results preserved.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency through explicit calibration details and instrument-response evidence, clarifies joint reconstruction, and resolves the TV-weight and runtime inconsistencies. Replacing the speculative 3D-extension discussion also better bounds the outlook. These are limited gains in documentation and internal consistency; retained benchmark results and the unexplained learning-rate reversal do not establish improved empirical performance.
